explanation: Reiniger animated The Adventures of Prince Achmed with cut-out silhouettes, moved frame by frame. It came out in 1926, 11 years before Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

claims.text: Lotte Reiniger's animated feature The Adventures of Prince Achmed premiered in 1926.
Disney's first animated feature, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, premiered in December 1937.
Reiniger animated Prince Achmed with cut-out silhouette figures, moved a little for each frame.
The Adventures of Prince Achmed was released 11 years before Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a detail is easy to get wrong; the schema's riskReason list has no 'only' or 'counterintuitive', so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Disney is the side most players pick, because Snow White is often thought of as the first animated feature; the gap is 11 years, so the answer holds whatever premiere date is used for either film. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: a German production set against a US one; no local knowledge is needed. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 28 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: the item deliberately makes no 'oldest surviving animated feature' claim for Prince Achmed, a superlative that would need its own evidence; seeded Hard and counterintuitive, as §8.2 requires.
